title: Adult anthropometry basis for belt and harness sizing
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Sizing the Hip Belt and Integrated Harness needs hip breadth, hip/waist circumference, thigh circumference, torso length and body mass percentiles. Open sources include CDC NHANES anthropometric reference data and the US Army ANSUR II public dataset.
objective: Extract 1st–99th percentile values for the relevant dimensions (male and female adults) from open sources, with the dataset version and licence.
acceptanceCriteria: Only openly licensed or public-domain sources; each value cites table/variable
Covers hip and waist circumference, hip breadth seated, thigh circumference, torso length (or best proxy), body mass
Notes known population biases (e.g., military sample)
